es.summary: La levotiroxina es una forma sintética de la hormona tiroidea T4 usada para reemplazar o suplementar la función tiroidea en pacientes con hipotiroidismo y para suprimir la TSH en cáncer de tiroides.
key_points: Se administra por vía oral, preferiblemente en ayunas y a la misma hora cada día.
La dosis se ajusta según TSH y T4 libre; el objetivo es normalizar el metabolismo basal.
Los efectos adversos de sobredosis incluyen taquicardia, arritmias y síntomas de hipertiroidismo.
Antácidos, calcio y hierro disminuyen su absorción; se deben espaciar 4 h.
En pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca o enfermedad coronaria, iniciar con dosis bajas para evitar sobrecarga metabólica.

mechanism: Proporciona T4 sintética que se convierte en T3 activa en tejidos periféricos.
T3 se une a receptores nucleares regulando la transcripción de genes metabólicos.
Aumenta el consumo de oxígeno y la producción de calor, elevando el metabolismo basal.
indications: Hipotiroidismo primario, secundario o terciario (incluye neonatos).
Supresión de TSH en cáncer de tiroides después de tiroidectomía o yodo radiactivo.
Tratamiento de bocio nodular y prevención de crecimiento de nódulos tiroideos.
contraindications: Infarto agudo de miocardio reciente o angina inestable.
Hipersensibilidad conocida a la levotiroxina o a excipientes.
adverse_effects: Intolerancia al calor, pérdida de peso, diarrea (comunes).
Osteoporosis y pérdida de masa ósea con uso prolongado (serio).
Síntomas de hipertiroidismo: sudoración, ansiedad, temblor (serio).
interactions: Antácidos, suplementos de calcio o hierro reducen la absorción; separar 4 h.
Warfarina: la levotiroxina puede potenciar el efecto anticoagulante.
Amiodarona y otros yoduros pueden alterar la función tiroidea.
Betabloqueantes pueden enmascarar taquicardia por sobredosis.
Simvastatina y otros fármacos metabolizados por CYP450 pueden requerir ajuste.
nursing_care: Evaluar TSH y T4 libre antes de iniciar y cada 6‑8 semanas tras ajustes.
Controlar frecuencia cardíaca, presión arterial y signos de hipertiroidismo.
Administrar la tableta con 200 mL de agua, en ayunas, 30‑60 min antes del desayuno.
Retener la dosis si el paciente presenta fiebre >38 °C, dolor torácico o arritmia.
Documentar cualquier cambio en peso, apetito o nivel de energía.
patient_teaching: Tomar la levotiroxina cada mañana con el estómago vacío y no comer durante 30‑60 min.
Evitar cambiar de marca sin consultar al médico.
Informar al profesional de salud si aparecen palpitaciones, temblores, dolor torácico o pérdida de peso rápida.
Acudir a los controles de laboratorio según lo indicado para ajustar la dosis.
Mantener una dieta equilibrada y evitar suplementos de calcio/ hierro cerca de la dosis.
antidote_overdose: No existe antídoto específico; tratar síntomas.
Soporte hemodinámico y monitoreo continuo de signos vitales.

outcomes: Paciente reportará disminución de la fatiga a ≤3/10 en escala de fatiga en 1 semana.
TSH del paciente se mantendrá dentro del rango objetivo (0.4‑4.0 µIU/mL) en 4‑6 semanas.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y signos de hipotiroidismo cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar mejoría o necesidad de ajuste de dosis.

interventions.action: Verificar resultados de TSH y T4 libre según orden médica.
interventions.rationale: Guía el ajuste de la levotiroxina para optimizar el metabolismo.

interventions.action: Administrar levotiroxina según prescripción, en ayunas y a la misma hora.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la absorción y mantiene niveles hormonales estables.

interventions.action: Monitorear frecuencia cardíaca y presión arterial cada 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Detecta efectos adversos de sobredosis o insuficiente reemplazo.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de la adherencia y los signos de sobredosis.
interventions.rationale: Facilita el autocuidado y la detección temprana de complicaciones.

en.summary: Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone T4 used to replace or supplement thyroid function in patients with hypothyroidism and to suppress TSH in thyroid cancer.
key_points: It is administered orally, preferably on an empty stomach and at the same time each day.
The dose is adjusted based on TSH and free T4; the goal is to normalize basal metabolism.
Overdose adverse effects include tachycardia, arrhythmias, and hyperthyroid symptoms.
Antacids, calcium, and iron decrease its absorption; they should be spaced 4 h apart.
In patients with heart failure or coronary artery disease, start with low doses to avoid metabolic overload.

mechanism: Provides synthetic T4 that is converted to active T3 in peripheral tissues.
T3 binds nuclear receptors regulating transcription of metabolic genes.
It increases oxygen consumption and heat production, raising basal metabolic rate.
indications: Primary, secondary, or tertiary hypothyroidism (including neonates).
TSH suppression in thyroid cancer after thyroidectomy or radioactive iodine.
Treatment of nodular goiter and prevention of thyroid nodule growth.
contraindications: Recent acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina.
Known hypersensitivity to levothyroxine or excipients.
adverse_effects: Osteoporosis and bone mass loss with prolonged use (serious).
interactions: Antacids, calcium or iron supplements reduce absorption; separate 4 h.
Warfarin: levothyroxine may potentiate anticoagulant effect.
Amiodarone and other iodides can alter thyroid function.
Beta‑blockers may mask tachycardia from overdose.
Simvastatin and other CYP450‑metabolized drugs may require adjustment.
nursing_care: Assess TSH and free T4 before starting and every 6‑8 weeks after adjustments.
Monitor heart rate, blood pressure, and signs of hyperthyroidism.
Administer tablet with 200 mL water, on an empty stomach, 30‑60 min before breakfast.
Hold dose if patient has fever >38 °C, chest pain, or arrhythmia.
Document any changes in weight, appetite, or energy level.
patient_teaching: Take levothyroxine each morning with an empty stomach and avoid eating for 30‑60 min.
Do not switch brands without consulting the physician.
Inform the healthcare provider if palpitations, tremors, chest pain, or rapid weight loss occur.
Attend laboratory checks as directed to adjust the dose.
Maintain a balanced diet and avoid calcium/iron supplements near dosing time.
antidote_overdose: Hemodynamic support and continuous vital sign monitoring.

outcomes: Patient will report a decrease in fatigue to ≤3/10 on the fatigue scale within 1 week.
Patient’s TSH will remain within the target range (0.4‑4.0 µIU/mL) in 4‑6 weeks.

interventions.action: Assess energy level and signs of hypothyroidism each shift.
interventions.rationale: Allows identification of improvement or need for dose adjustment.

interventions.action: Verify TSH and free T4 results per physician order.
interventions.rationale: Guides levothyroxine adjustment to optimize metabolism.

interventions.action: Administer levothyroxine as prescribed, on an empty stomach and at the same time.
interventions.rationale: Improves absorption and maintains stable hormone levels.

interventions.action: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure every 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Detects adverse effects of overdose or inadequate replacement.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of adherence and signs of overdose.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates self‑care and early detection of complications.

summary.0.quote: Levothyroxine sodium tablets are a L-thyroxine (T4) indicated in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates, for: Hypothyroidism: As replacement therapy in primary (thyroidal), secondary (pituitary), and tertiary (hypothalamic) congenital or acquired hypothyroidism.

key_points.2.quote: The signs and symptoms of overdosage are those of hyperthyroidism [see Warnings and Precautions (5) and Adverse Reactions (6) ] .

key_points.3.quote: Instruct patients not to take levothyroxine sodium tablets within 4 hours of these agents.

key_points.4.quote: Initiate levothyroxine sodium therapy in this population at lower doses than those recommended in younger individuals or in patients without cardiac disease [see Dosage and Administration (2.3) and Use in Specific Populations (8.5) ].

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Triiodothyronine (T3) and L-thyroxine (T4) diffuse into the cell nucleus and bind to thyroid receptor proteins attached to DNA.

sections.indications.0.quote: Levothyroxine sodium tablets are indicated in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates, as a replacement therapy in primary (thyroidal), secondary (pituitary), and tertiary (hypothalamic) congenital or acquired hypothyroidism.

sections.indications.1.quote: Levothyroxine sodium tablets are indicated in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates, as an adjunct to surgery and radioiodine therapy in the management of thyrotropin-dependent well-differentiated thyroid cancer.

sections.indications.2.quote: Levothyroxine sodium tablets are not indicated for suppression of benign thyroid nodules and nontoxic diffuse goiter in iodine-sufficient patients as there are no clinical benefits and overtreatment with levothyroxine sodium may induce hyperthyroidism [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ].

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Cardiovascular: palpitations, tachycardia, arrhythmias, increased pulse and blood pressure, heart failure, angina, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest Resp

sections.adverse_effects.4.quote: They include the following: General: fatigue, increased appetite, weight loss, heat intolerance, fever, excessive sweating Central nervous system: headache, hyperactivity, nervousness, anxiety, irritability, emotional lability, insomnia Musculoskeletal: tremors, muscle weakness, muscle spasm Cardiovascular: palpitations, tachycardia, arrhythmias, increased pulse and blood pressure, heart failure, angina, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest Resp

sections.interactions.0.quote: Instruct patients not to take levothyroxine sodium tablets within 4 hours of these agents.

sections.interactions.1.quote: Levothyroxine sodium increases the response to oral anticoagulant therapy.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: Monitor TSH and total or free-T4 in pediatric patients as follows: 2 and 4 weeks after the initiation of treatment, 2 weeks after any change in dosage, and then every 3 to 12 months thereafter following dosage stabilization until growth is completed.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Instruct patients to notify their healthcare provider if they experience any of the following symptoms: rapid or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, shortness of breath, leg cramps, headache, nervousness, irritability, sleeplessness, tremors, change in appetite, weight gain or loss, vomiting, diarrhea, excessive sweating, heat intolerance, fever, changes in menstrual periods, hives or skin rash, or any other unusual medical event.
